rows.en: <operator(14030,1)><speed(2)>That <color(5)>Berkt<ce()> guy is a real pain. To think he can move the boss's own forces...
<operator(17040,1)><speed(2)>That's what you'd expect from a <color(5)>New Federation<ce()> executive. He must've put in a word with <color(5)>Bloodman<ce()>.
rows.notes: 'Bloodman' used as short form of the locked 'Fixx Bloodman' (encyclopedia_021_a/022); no dialogue precedent yet for the short form.

rows.en: <operator(21020,1)><speed(2)>So they decided it was too dangerous to leave us running free.
<operator(23030,1)><speed(2)>Guess that makes us the most troublesome elite unit the <color(5)>New Federation<ce()>'s got to deal with.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)><color(5)>Berkt<ce()>...
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>Still bothered by it, <color(4)>Barrel<ce()>?
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>When I saw him... I felt it. That he's someone almost exactly like me.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>But what he's trying to do...
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>I know he's a bad guy. But... somehow I'm scared to find out more about him.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>...Makes me wonder if it's really okay to keep fighting like this.
<operator(19010,1)><speed(2)>Don't look away.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>Huh?
<operator(23030,1)><speed(2)>That's right. If it really bothers you, then chase him down. Don't beg for it - go after it yourself.
rows.notes: Echoes but is not identical to the locked Eureka Seven motto; this source line ('nedaruna, motomeru nda') is shorter and distinct, translated on its own terms.

rows.en: <operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>Yes...
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>...
<operator(23010,1)><speed(2)>I don't really know what to say, but...
<operator(21010,1)><speed(2)>No matter what happens, we're on your side. Just know that much, okay?
<operator(17010,1)><speed(2)>Don't know anything about his deal, but you're you.
<operator(1040,2)><speed(2)>...Thanks. With everyone here, I feel like I can keep fighting.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>Boys and their friendship, huh...
<operator(23010,1)><speed(2)>We have to protect the <color(4)>Gekko<ce()> no matter what!
<operator(23020,1)><speed(2)>Yeah...
<operator(23010,1)><speed(2)>...Is the <color(4)>Nirvash<ce()> still not doing well?
<operator(23020,1)><speed(2)>Yeah. If we could, I wanted to get it looked at first.
<operator(23010,1)><speed(2)>But the enemy's...
<operator(23020,1)><speed(2)>I know. I'll ask it to hang in there through this fight somehow.
<operator(23010,1)><speed(2)>Let's get this fight over with fast and get the <color(4)>Nirvash<ce()> looked at properly.
<operator(23020,1)><speed(2)>Yeah.
<operator(19030,1)><speed(2)>And here I thought we'd get a breather! Give me a break, seriously!
<operator(19020,1)><speed(2)>Then let's hurry up and finish it off.
<operator(19030,1)><speed(2)>Like it's gonna be that easy!?
<operator(19060,1)><speed(2)>No, <color(4)>Kei<ce()>'s right. Drag this out and the <color(4)>Gekko<ce()>'s in danger. Let's finish it fast!
<operator(19030,1)><speed(2)>Yeah, yeah. Geez... the old man's soft on <color(4)>Kei<ce()>. Textbook doting parent, that guy.
<operator(19060,1)><speed(2)>You say something!?
<operator(12061,2)><speed(2)>Just occurred to me, but there's a lot of interesting machines in this world, huh?
<operator(19030,1)><speed(2)>Guess you're right about that. I mean, <color(4)>Shin Getter<ce()> combines AND transforms.
<operator(12061,1)><speed(2)>Lucky~! So cool, exactly like Gekiganger! Wish the <color(4)>Aestivalis<ce()> could at least combine too.
<operator(12071,1)><speed(2)>If it could... now that'd be a real blessing.
rows.notes: Source line reads as wordplay (Izumi is written as an incurable punster); exact pun not recoverable, meaning kept plain.

rows.en: <operator(6011,1)><speed(2)>KLF flight path prediction, repurposing <color(4)>Nirvash<ce()> data.
rows.notes: Speaker id 6011 resolves to Heero Yuy; these lines read as a terse onboard-computer readout, matching his stoic voice.

rows.en: <operator(6011,1)><speed(2)>For <color(5)>New Federation<ce()> mass-production types, reusing <color(4)>Terminus<ce()> data with a 30 percent downward correction applied.
<operator(6011,1)><speed(2)>The black KLF... applying <color(4)>Nirvash<ce()> sample values across all its data.
rows.notes: 'KLF' left untranslated, parallel to how 'LFO' is kept elsewhere; no locked expansion or spelling found.

rows.en: <operator(6011,1)><speed(2)>Correction complete. Saving data. ...Combat prep, complete.
<operator(23100,1)><speed(2)>It's your first time in another world - aren't you even a little surprised?
<operator(6011,1)><speed(2)>I do what needs doing... that's all.
<operator(23100,1)><speed(2)>Tch, you're no fun~!
<operator(14010,1)><speed(2)>So this is the other world, huh... Feels like something out of sci-fi.
<operator(14030,1)><speed(2)>No kidding. Being this different, it feels like we landed on another planet.
<operator(14010,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Marina<ce()>, you look pretty down.
<operator(1020,1)><speed(2)>It's only that... it brought back the last war. I didn't want to fight again...
<operator(14010,1)><speed(2)>But we have to get through it. To grab a better future.
<operator(1020,1)><speed(2)>...Yeah, you're right!
<operator(14030,1)><speed(2)>Let's give this so-called <color(5)>New Federation<ce()> a proper greeting!

uncertainties.issue: 'Bloodman' as short form of the locked 'Fixx Bloodman': no dialogue precedent, only encyclopedia full-name entries.
Holland's line is a shorter, different phrasing from the locked full Eureka Seven motto ('Don't beg for things. Do it yourself...'); translated on its own rather than substituting the locked wording.
Izumi's source line appears to be a pun (she is written as an incurable punster); rendered plainly as 'a real blessing'.
Speaker id 6011 resolves to Heero Yuy via speaker_lookup.py; rows read like an onboard AI/computer readout rather than ordinary speech, kept literal and terse to match.
'KLF' left untranslated (parallel to 'LFO' elsewhere in the corpus); no locked expansion or spelling found in the glossary files.
